newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's P.W.Botha refuses apology for apartheid.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's P.W.Botha refuses apology for apartheid.

text.p: Former South African president P.W. Botha declared on Thursday he would never apologise for apartheid and denounced what he called an unforgiving assault on the Afrikaner by the country's new black rulers.

"I am not guilty of any deed for which I should apologise or ask for amnesty. I therefore have no intention of doing this," Botha, one of the last two surviving white apartheid presidents, said in a statement after a meeting with Archbishop Desmond Tutu.

"I am deeply concerned about the fierce and unforgiving assault which is being launched against the Afrikaner and his language at all levels of society," said Botha, who became prime minister in 1978.
The post was converted to a presidency in 1984. Botha stepped down in 1989 and was replaced by F.W. de Klerk who was ousted in South Africa's first all race election in 1994.

Botha said in his statement he had never associated himself with "blatant murder". "It would however now appear that there might have been instances during the conflict of the past where individuals have exceeded the limits of their authority," he said.

Tutu, chairman of South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission which is probing apartheid human rights abuses, asked for the meeting in the coastal town of George where Botha has a retirement home.
